Question: Do Indian actors refuse to work with Pakistani actresses? If so, why?
Answer: They generally didn’t used to, especially prior to 2016. Many actors have appeared opposite Pakistani actresses. This list includes pairs such as Shah Rukh Khan & Mahira Khan, Mithun Chakraborty & Salma Agha , Saif Ali Khan & Somy Ali, Ashmit Patel & Meera, Himesh Reshammiya & Sara Loren, Harshwardhan Rane & Mawra Hocane, and Irrfan Khan & Saba Qamar, etc etc etc. But then the Uri terror attack happened in 2016, and Pakistani actors were banned in Bollywood movies. Then the 2019 Pulwama terror attack happened, and the All Indian Cine Workers Association announced a total ban on all Pakistani actors and artists. As of today, the ban is still in effect - so, even if Indian actors would want to work with Pakistani actresses, they would probably not be able to do so, unless the ban is lifted. And, till the ban is lifted, Indian movie producers aren’t going to be very keen on casting Pakistani actresses in their films.

Question: Is a king cobra more dangerous than other cobras?
Answer: A King Cobra is terribly dangerous for cobras, while the proletariat or less-royal cobras are terribly dangerous for us hapless human beings. Of course, a King Cobra can easily kill a human with a single bite; however, King Cobras simply aren’t as dangerous for humans primarily because human-KC interactions are quite rare. King Cobras live very deep in the jungles, and very few naive humans usually hang around in those parts (those parts have a noticeable lack of ‘bars’, so it’s difficult to buy a beer or do a livestream to influence others there). It’s usually experts there who know how to handle the snakes and themselves. Also, consider this - you and I are in considerably more danger of being mugged or assaulted by some ordinary lout than we are of being assaulted or mugged by Prince Charles or some other Royal, right? Additionally, Kings are not as skittish as regular cobras are. The Spectacled cobra on the other hand is a proud member of the Big 4 of venomous snakes, which together kill more than 50,000 people annually in the greater Indian subcontinent. Kings barely kill a couple of people here and there, and a majority of times, those people are the ones who try to “kiss” the King Cobras. Consent is a rather important concept, isn’t it? Can’t say I blame the Kings here. To sum it all - King Cobras are not as dangerous as the regular common cobras. This is primarily due to the fact that regular cobras hang around people a lot more and are loads more skittish and bite people significantly more. But of course, the mighty mosquito is the most deadly and dangerous of all, and it isn’t even a snake.

Question: What is the meaning of the popular song ‘Oo Antava’ from the movie ‘Pushpa’ that features famous actors Allu Arjun and Samantha? Why has it been dubbed into so many other Indian regional languages? Do you like the song?
Answer: That particular song is essentially a raunchy item song. It is being marketed and talked about like it’s some sort of feminist empowering song with a social message. However, dressing up a crocodile in a Chanel outfit does not change the fact that we’re still looking at a crocodile. The song is essentially about how girls and women are ogled and catcalled at by boys and men throughout their lives, and how no matter how the girl or woman is, there will be some lad or man waiting in the wings, ready to shower his (un)wanted attentions on that girl or woman. Why was it dubbed into so many languages? That was more because the movie was dubbed into many languages, so they went the whole hog, and got it sung in other languages too. Do I like the song? It’s alright - I don’t love it but I don’t hate it either. The makers shouldn’t have tried to justify it by calling it a “social message song”. It’s a raunchy item song, and no amount of dressing it up is going to make it a “social message song”. They ought to have been honest and said, “Yeah, it’s an item song! Don’t like it? Then, don’t watch it! But we know, you will!”

Question: Did Anushka Sharma come from a rich family or was she poor to afford her education & lifestyle before entering into films?
Answer: Anushka Sharma did not come from a super rich affluent family, but she didn’t come from a humble background either. Her dad was an Indian Army officer, and her mother was a homemaker. She was not poor in terms of not being able to afford an education, but she wasn’t living the kind of ultra luxurious lifestyle she has now. So, it’s not like she was being driven around in Range Rovers or Mercedese Benzes or BMWs, or vacationing in Paris or Sydney or Malé. But she definitely was not poor - maybe so in comparison with her current net worth. And she did not grow up in the lap of luxury like many of her contemporaries did. One could classify her as growing up in a middle-class or even upper-middle-class family so to speak. Definitely not poor, and definitely not ultra wealthy. But of course, her family would be considered rich if compared to a poverty struck family. So, it’s all relative, I guess. But overall, middle-class or upper middle-class is what one would consider her family’s wealth status. Things have obviously changed for the better now for everyone in her family.

Question: Did you like the Animal movie? Was it similar or better than Kabir Singh?
Answer: Personally I liked Animal a lot more than I did Kabir Singh. Oddly though, Kabir Singh is actually the movie with a more cohesive script and storyline. I guess I liked Animal more because I like its cast more. And even though both movie protagonists are violent and aggressive, somehow I found Ranvijay Singh more simpatico than I did Kabir Singh. I guess it also helps that I like Ranbir Kapoor a lot - while I like Shahid Kapoor too, I like Ranbir much more. And, Bobby Deol is amazing too in a tiny role! There is also the fact that Animal has a more escapist theme in its plot. I mean many of the scenes in it are pure escapist fantasy (e.g. the huge machine gun scene and the Mano-y-mano fight between Bobby and Ranbir). In contrast, Kabir Singh feels much more realistic. And oh boy, the BGM in Animal is brilliant! So, yes I liked Animal, and I think while there are some similarities between Animal and Kabir Singh, they are two entirely different movies. You will like one over the other depending on which actor/actress you like more, and if you like realism or escapism in your cinema. Of course, you may hate both films too - in which case, perhaps you should avoid watching Sandeep Reddy Vanga films in the future.

Question: How come Bollywood actors and actresses have such an excellent command over the English language?

Generally speaking, many of the lot who have gone abroad to study, tend to have a decent command over English, and can converse with ease. If you hear them speak in their native tongues (be it Hindi or Gujarati or Tamil or Bengali, etc.) you’ll see how flawlessly and poetically they speak those tongues. So, I’d say that some are indeed fluent in English, but that doesn’t apply to all Bollywood actors and actresses.

Question: Is Ranbir Kapoor's "Brahmastra" a flop movie?
Answer: We are peering into the (not-so-distant but nevertheless the) future here, since Bhramastra has not yet released. It releases in September, so there’s like two more months before we see whether or not it is a flop. Personally speaking, I am pretty confident that I will like the movie. It’s got actors I really like, such as Ranbir Kapoor, Amitabh Bachchan and Alia Bhatt. However, I am not as confident about my ability to predict its box office potential. There is a lot of finickiness in Indian movie audiences. They reject some really great movies, and then flock to some absolute mediocre fare. There is also the fact that Sci-Fi just hasn’t typically gotten great reactions among Indian audiences, so this was always a risky move. Finally, the many years of making have obviously bloated its budget - so, even if it does well, it may never recoup its cost. That could then result in a similar fate that befell Jagga Jasoos (which I personally adored!) So, while it’s not yet a flop movie, there are definitely prospects of it becoming a flop. I would of course prefer that it’s not, but I am not representative of the entire segment of movie going audiences. Let’s hope it does exceedingly well, but if it doesn’t, then I’m afraid the movie may well end up as a flop.

Question: What are some non-venomous snake species that can be dangerous to humans? Can these snakes be kept as pets?
Answer: The giant constrictor type of snakes can be dangerous to humans. The top two would probably be the African Rock Python and the Reticulated Python. Both Python varieties can grow to ridiculously large sizes, and are capable of easily asphyxiating humans, and in some cases, eating them up (at least smaller sized humans - even a huge Python would struggle to swallow up an Andre the Giant sized human). They have been kept as pets, but experts suggest that it is highly risky to keep these two varieties as pets. If you want to keep a Python as a pet, get a Ball Python. But I do know of people who keep these giant varieties as pets, and I always wonder why. Especially because the African Rock Python is one of the meanest snakes out there, and is likely to attack you right out of its eggshell (as a herpetologist sardonically said in an interview). But these are my top two picks for dangerous non-venomous snakes that should not be kept as pets.

Question: What is the danger of handling a black mamba?
Answer: The biggest danger is of course that the Mamba bites the bejesus out of you. Two drops of Mamba venom are quite enough to kill an adult human being. Some of the usual symptoms involve “pleasant symptoms” like paralysis, hyper-salivation, dizziness, and hemorrhage. Oh, and it’s going to pain worse than a dentist yanking your teeth out with a blunt rusty spanner. Then, if you don’t get rushed to the hospital, and heaven forbid, they don’t have any antivenom, then by golly, you are definitely dead. Handling the Black Mamba casually is a recipe for disaster, and one may as well arrange for one’s last will to be arranged beforehand. Handling a Black Mamba (by a nonexpert) is basically seeking out an appointment with death.

Question: Why has Vidya Balan never worked with Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, and Aamir Khan?
Answer: She’s just never been offered a role opposite any of the trio. For better or for worse, Vidya Balan has slotted herself into a “serious actress” category. Our Khan trio rarely if ever make uber-serious movies. So, at the outset, there just isn’t a natural fit. Likewise, Vidya Balan is now 43 years old, which makes her significantly younger than our Khan triumvirate, who are all in their upper-50s. But in most movie industries’ logic, an actress who is 40+ is almost always “aged out”. Our Khan trio (especially Aamir and Salman) come with really younger actresses, so Vidya is out of luck there. So, unless the Khan trio make an uber-realistic movie, there really is no chance of seeing Vidya Balan appearing opposite them. Out of the trio though, I think the best prospects are to see her with Shahrukh, but those are pretty low too. So, I suppose, we just have to be satisfied to see her with Shahrukh during the latter’s cameo in Heyy Baby.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Did Jennifer Lawrence sleep her way to the top?
Answer: Well, if JLaw slept on her way to the top, then by golly, she must be an expert in sleepwalking. I mean, imagine sleepwalking all the way to the top of various buildings. The mind boggles imagining her extreme dexterity in doing that. Fabulous! I guess all that training for Red Sparrow and The Hunger Games paid off! But jokes apart, I think she was very much awake, on her way to the top. One can hardly sleep while traipsing up stairs, all the way to the top of various high rise buildings, eh? I would not recommend it at all. So, please people, if you’re on your way to the top, don’t sleep on your way up. After you reach the top of the building, then yes, by all means, take a power nap, or a siesta, or what have you! But don’t sleep on your way up - you’ll take an unfortunate tumble!

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Megan Fox the most beautiful woman in the world?
Answer: Maybe she isn’t for some, maybe she is for some. But she is definitely the most beautiful woman in the world for her present fiancé, Machine Gun Kelly. Based on their various interactions and Instagram posts, it looks like he’s the most handsome man in the world, as per her, as well. And, I’m sure that there are plenty of diehard Megan Fox fans who will also consider her to be the most beautiful woman in the world. But really, this is a question seeking an objective answer to a rather subjective question - the answer is, it depends on who’s evaluating the question. If MGK is, then we know that she is definitely the Queen of his heart.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: If a European actor or actress with dark hair and dark eyes is hired to play an Indian (desi) role, is it possible for the actor or actress to act like a real Indian so that the audience will mistake the actor for an Indian actor or actress?
Answer: I think many in the audience may well think that the actor or actress is Indian. Although, I think this may work out better with actresses than actors - there are several actresses in Indian movies, who are European or have European ancestry. I can’t say the same applies for actors though. For instance, Amy Jackson has come in several movies as an Indian character in them. Ditto for Katrina Kaif, Elly AvRam, Yana Gupta, and Kristina Akheeva. They’ve all come at different times essaying Indian characters. If one doesn’t look too closely, they’re all passable as Indians. There’s also the niggling fact though that many of these actresses usually get small roles (not Katrina nowadays though), and most just come for songs and dances. If they played meatier roles, then perhaps the subterfuge wouldn’t work. But for the roles they do, they do pass off as Indian.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What are some movies that have to do with food?
Answer: There are lots of movies about food - my favorite one which features food in practically every major scene is the Japanese film Tampopo. A brilliant and exceedingly funny movie, that one! It’s awesome! Watch it for sure! There’s also a couple of Bollywood films about food. Two that come to mind are Daawat-e-Ishq and Luv Shuv Tey Chicken Khurana. Both are decent enough but neither can match up to Tampopo. Definitely watch Tampopo - it’ll make you crave Ramen although you may not crave Oysters as much after watching it ;)

Answer: Vulgarity is very much in the eye of judgmental beholders. I personally never ever knock anyone’s choices in sartorial styles. After all, if someone likes and is comfy in a particular dress or outfit, then who are we to comment on the supposed ‘vulgarity’ of that outfit? If one doesn’t like that dress, then by all means, do not wear it yourself. Take a gander at the five actresses above - these are some of their outfits that seem to have attracted the displeasure of lots of opinionated online fashionistas. The common refrain among those critics is that these outfits are “vulgar”. I on the other hand have no such judgment to pass. To me, it looks like these actresses liked what they were wearing. So, let it be, eh? I do not believe in condemning others choices as vulgar, just because some obnoxious hidebound critics think they are. At least, the actresses aren’t forcing anyone else to wear what they are, right?

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Which movie will you watch Akshay Kumar's Raksha Bandhan or Aamir Khan Lal Singh Chadda since both are releasing on 11th of August?
Answer: Neither movie really appeals to me - one is going to be a boring remake of one of the most recognizable movies of all time. And, the trailer basically makes it look like PK has returned with a luxurious beard, to roam around planet earth again. Come on Aamir, couldn’t you make a movie with an original story? I’d love to see another Talaash or Sarfarosh from you, instead of seeing you constantly as a mentally challenged naive innocent character. The other is going to be a thinly disguised social issues movie masquerading as a comedy. Aanand L. Rai needs to get out of his comfort zone a bit now. All his movies are beginning to look like and feel the same. And Akki, please make a straight out masala action flick now - enough with the biopics and social issues flicks. Your hardcore original fanbase (I am one in that group) liked you because you were an action star - give us a couple of flicks like that. How impossible is it for you to toss us a Rowdy Rathore or a Sooryavanshi with more regularity? So, to sum it up - I’ll watch both movies grudgingly, and I am definitely not watching either in the theatre. Nope, I’ll wait for them to come on some streaming channel first.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: What are the chances of a love story between Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt in "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil"?
Answer: The chances of a love story between Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt in Ae Dil Hai Mushkil is perilously close to zero. That’s because that movie has already been completed and released six years ago. So, at this point it is practically impossible for KJo to reshoot that film and release it again. However, there can be a decent possibility that a sequel could be made for ADHM, where our Ranbir Kapoor’s character Ayan has a love story with Alia Bhatt’s DJ Alia character. I would certainly not be averse to seeing a sequel to ADHM with the lead pair of Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt. It might be a good movie, but I’m not sure KJo has any plans for doing that. Someone should ask him and see if he’s open to making a sequel of ADHM with Ranbir and Alia. It might be a worthwhile project to make next.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why does the new Bollywood celeb Disha Patani have more Instagram likes than other established actresses?
Answer: Well, she’s not really a new celeb any longer. She’s fairly seasoned now, any way you look at it. She’s been around for six years now, and in these six years, she has firmly established herself as the most glamorous Bollywood celebrity out there. It certainly helps that she is the face of Calvin Klein in India. As far as Instagram likes are concerned - if you would simply go to her profile, you’ll see why she gets so many likes. Typically, the more glamorous a female celebrity, and her pictures and videos are, the more likes she will get. That’s pretty much it. Most of the more established Bollywood celebs are nowhere near the glamor levels of Disha Patani. They are all a lot more conservative in terms of glamour quotient when compared with Disha.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Why is it so difficult for Bollywood actors and actresses to wear sarees perfectly well?
Answer: Dear QPG, it is actually not difficult at all for Bollywood actresses to wear sarees. They seem to be pretty adept at doing so. Yes, the actors may have a harder time doing so, but they’ve also donned sarees, especially when they appear in drag in some movie roles. But most actresses seem to have little to no trouble in this department. Also, even if they are unable to don it on their own, there’s always an obliging assistant to help them. So, it isn’t really a big deal! They seem to all wear them with relative ease.

Name: Aditya Simha
Question: Is Talia al Ghul a good guy or a bad guy?
Answer: Well, for starters, unless they are planning a massive and bound to be unpopular retcon of sorts, Talia is not really a guy at all. She’s always been depicted as a beautiful and dangerously capable woman in all the Batman comics. As far as being a villain is concerned, sometimes she’s a villain and sometimes she’s not. She’s not a villain like the Joker for instance - sometimes, she’s even helped Batman and friends. But all things considered, she is a bit of both. Sometimes good, and sometimes bad - but from a purely moral standpoint, she is rather steeped in crime.
